score.residual: The dominant remaining defect is a single, isolated register-allocation choice: the reference keeps the 48-frame loop counter in r7 (a low register, reusing the same r7 that briefly held work+0x7828's address at the very start, before that value's last use at the field-0x24 read preceding the loop) and tests it with a bare `cmp r7,#48; bne.n <loop>`. This compiler instead keeps the loop counter in a high register (r8) for this owner, which cannot be compared against an 8-bit immediate directly in Thumb, so the back edge costs three extra instructions (`movs r2,#1; add r8,r2; mov r3,r8` in place of a single `adds r7,#1`) and a different two-branch shape (`beq.n <exit>; b.n <loop>` in place of one `bne.n <loop>`), worth roughly 8 of the 20 extra candidate bytes. This is the same category of residual already recorded on sibling owners in this exact 0x03001eec family -- games/gs1/recon/en/main/080dc1ec.json and 080d59b0.json both document this compiler choosing a different high register than the reference for a value that must stay live across the owner's whole body, confirmed there (and reconfirmed here) to be insensitive to declaration order, block scope, and loop-statement shape. Not pursued further per the project's ban on forcing register assignment or running an open-ended permutation search for this category of mismatch. The remaining ~12 bytes are the ordinary knock-on pool-offset churn that follows from this one upstream register choice cascading through the rest of the function's pc-relative loads.

Semantic summary: a second battle-presentation sub-effect sharing the 0x03001eec work block with member_orbit. Republishes its object argument at work+0x7828, loads up to three palettes (a third only when mode==2) into BG palette RAM, computes a BG2 affine scale and reference-point pair from a single object field via EffectPosition_ApplyAlternateStepAndYOffset (0x100/1.0 scale when mode==0, a smaller Value_000000cc scale with a Func_080022ec-derived reference point otherwise), registers two rectangle-blit routines (heap kinds 46 and 47) and a per-frame callback, sets the mode-dependent impact-mode field (0x77A8), then runs a fixed 48 frames: a target-id notify on frame 0 (Func_080d6888, argument set differing by mode), fixed sound/message cues on frames 8 and 24, and -- for frames 0-27 -- two rectangle draws per frame through the two staged draw callbacks, positioned and sized from three small lookup tables at 0x080EE096/0x080EE09C/0x080EE09F indexed by a frame/4-derived, collapsed-to-{0,1,2} radius index.

Field offset 0x24 (36) on the object at work+0x7828 is read as a plain scalar s16 throughout (not, as in the template, the start of a member-id array), consistent with this being a single-target rather than whole-party effect.
